Open Start and type your farm name and your own limits in the yellow cells: rain that stops work, wind limits, frost, safe grain moisture, rate error, days between calibrations and tank size.
Keep Operator Hours and Crop Growth Stages up to date first: staff with phone and cost, and one row for every field with its crop, area, supervisor, growth stage and planned harvest date.
Log every job on Field Operations Log with task, field, machine, operator, hours, area and fuel. Cost, cost per hectare and the rain of the day fill in.
Record each sowing on Sowing Records and each spray on Spray Records with product, dose, area, wind, batch and the label intervals. Missing data and strong wind are flagged.
Write scouting walks on Scouting Reports and set your action levels on Action Thresholds. Reports at or above the threshold turn red and show the product to use.
Read Pre-harvest Interval before every harvest: it shows the earliest harvest date and the re-entry date for each field and warns when the planned date is too early.
Log every weighed load on Harvest Loads and every harvest day on Harvest Crew Hours. Yield per Field then shows tonnes, yield, the gap to your target and the value.
Enter the weather each day on Weather Log, the field gauges on Rain Gauge per Field and frost, hail and storms on Frost Hail and Storms. Days lost to weather are counted.
Plan the week on Weekly Work Orders, write the diary on Farm Diary, and keep Calibration Records, Crop Loss and Replanting, Contractor Work and Weed Control Log up to date.

Use the 14 calculators for spray mix, sprayer calibration, area per hour, harvest forecast, interval check, seed rate, moisture shrink, harvest loss, weeding labour, work plan, yield, weather delay, tank refills and cost per hectare.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to open WhatsApp with the text ready.
Read Field Operations Dashboard and Charts every week: sprays, intervals, scouting, loads, yield against target, weather and hours.
Track inputs, fertiliser, chemicals, water and pumps in one workbook
Control inputs, fertiliser, chemicals, water and pump cost
Stock reorder point with days of cover
opening stock, purchases, applications and issues give each input's balance, days of cover and an order quantity once it falls below your reorder point
kilograms of N, P2O5 and K2O planned for each field are set against what fertiliser and manure have put on, with a warning when a field goes over
each fertiliser price is divided by its nitrogen, phosphate and potash share so you can compare urea, compound and potash on what the nutrient really costs
Supplier quotes ranked on landed price
price plus transport is ranked for every input, with the extra you would pay against the best quote and the cost per kg of nutrient
the last recorded spray of each product on each crop gives the first safe harvest day and flags crops you must not harvest yet
Irrigation schedule with next turn and hours
depth, interval and the flow of the water source give the water and pump hours for a turn and the date of the next turn for every field
water pumped from every borehole, intake and canal turn is added up against its yearly quota, with licence end and pump service warnings
meter readings are compared with the hours you logged, and the water applied is compared with the crop need after usable rain
Pump energy cost per m3 and per mm
kilowatt hours and your tariff give the energy cost of every pump and week, the cost of each cubic metre and a warning above your limit
Input cost per hectare against budget
seed, fertiliser, protection and fuel issued to each field are added up and set against the budget per hectare you set
on-time and in-full deliveries, price against your list and days to pay are worked out for every supplier and rated reliable, watch or poor
every batch has its hazard class and expiry date, and expired or soon-to-expire products are flagged for return or safe disposal

Input price list with price change and nutrient cost
One row for each input with unit, price now, price last season, supplier and the share of nitrogen, phosphate and potash; price change, stock, cost per kg of nutrient and season spend fill in.
Supplier performance: on time, in full, price
One row for each supplier with contact and payment terms; orders, deliveries, share on time and in full, price against your list and a rating fill in from the orders and purchases.
One row for each invoice line with date, input, supplier, invoice number, quantity, price and the day you paid; cost, price against your list, due date and payment check fill in.
Input stock by store: opening, in, used and balance
One row for each tracked input with its store, opening stock, reorder point and the last count; stock in, used, balance, value, days of cover, count difference and a reorder check fill in.
Input use per field: what was issued to which field
One row for each issue from the store with date, field, input, crop, quantity and who took it; unit, price, cost and category fill in.
Input cost per hectare for every field against its budget
One row for each field with area, supervisor, crop and the budget per hectare; season cost of seed, fertiliser, protection and other inputs, cost per hectare and a budget check fill in.
Fertiliser plan: N, P2O5 and K2O for each field
One row for each field with the kilograms of N, P2O5 and K2O per hectare you plan; area, totals, what fertiliser and manure have already put on, the nitrogen balance and a plan check fill in.
N applied for the field, kg
Fertiliser applications: field, product and rate
One row for each application with date, field, fertiliser, method and rate in kg per hectare; kilograms, cost, nitrogen, phosphate and potash supplied and whether the field has a plan fill in.
Manure and compost: tonnes and nutrients spread
One row for each spreading with field, kind, tonnes and the kilograms of N, P2O5 and K2O in a tonne; nutrients for the field, per hectare and their worth in fertiliser fill in.
One row for each crop and product with the stage, dose per hectare, number of sprays and the days between them; cost per hectare, withholding period and a check against the label limits fill in.
One row for each product and crop with the days to wait before harvest, the most sprays and the largest dose on the label; the last spray you recorded, the first safe harvest day and a check fill in.
One row for each input and month with the price you paid or were quoted; the change from last month, the change from a year ago and a price check fill in.
One row for each quote with vendor, quantity, price, transport, validity and lead time; landed price, total, the best quote, the extra you would pay and the cost per kg of nutrient fill in.
Input orders and deliveries: promised, received and late
One row for each order with supplier, input, quantity, price, the promised date, the delivery date and the quantity received; value, days late, share delivered and a delivery check fill in.
Chemical store register: batches, hazard and expiry
One row for each batch in the chemical store with product, batch number, hazard class, dates, quantity, shelf and storekeeper; days to expiry, value and an expiry check fill in.
Water sources: flow, quota, licence and pump service

One row for each borehole, intake, canal turn, dam or tank with flow, yearly quota, licence, pump service date and contacts; water used this season, share of quota, licence and service checks fill in.
Irrigation schedule per field: depth, interval and next turn
One row for each irrigated field with water source, depth per turn, days between turns, season dates and contractor; water and hours for a turn, the last run, the next turn and a check fill in.
Irrigation log: hours run and water applied
One row for each irrigation run with date, field, water source, hours run, any issue and the day it was fixed; cubic metres, millimetres applied and a status fill in.
Pump runs and energy cost per week
One row for each pump and week with the start time, hours run and kilowatt hours used; water pumped, energy cost, cost per cubic metre and per mm on a hectare and a check fill in.

Hello, we order {qty_ordered} {unit} of {item} at {price} per {unit}, a value of {value}. Order number {ord_id}. Please confirm the order and the delivery date.
Hello, we expect {item} ({qty_ordered} {unit}) on {promised}. Please tell us the time of day. Our store takes deliveries between 7:00 and 16:00.
Hello, order {ord_id} for {item} arrived with {qty_received} {unit} instead of {qty_ordered}. Please send the rest this week or issue a credit note.
Hello {vendor}, please send your best price for {qty} of {item}, delivered to our farm, with the lead time and how long the quote is valid. Your last quote was {price} per unit.
Hello, invoice {invoice} for {item} charges {price} per unit but our list price is {list_price}. Please check it and send a corrected invoice.
Hello, batch {batch} of {item} expired on {expiry}. We hold {qty} {unit}. Can you take it back or tell us how to dispose of it safely?

Hello, the fertiliser plan for {field} ({crop}, {area} ha) is ready: N {n_ha}, P2O5 {p_ha} and K2O {k_ha} kg per ha. Please check it before we order the fertiliser.

Hello, please read the water meter on {field} today and send me the number. The last reading was {now_read} m3 on {now_date}.
